description: Update the architecture spec to reflect the redesigned chat surface, welcome screen + nav restructure, and the three new functionality features (attach/upload, repository context, pluggable web search). This keeps .kiro/specs/hybrid-orchestrator/architecture.md the source of truth and records the concrete mechanisms + the error->warning-icon->modal UX + secret handling. Do this LAST so it documents what actually shipped.
steps: Edit .kiro/specs/hybrid-orchestrator/architecture.md Section 8.1 (Chat interface): document the bottom-anchored composer with compact inline controls (inline model selector, inline routing-mode control, 'Why this model?' info icon, Attach/Repository/Web-search toggle icons, Send/Stop, Refresh icon), and that the always-on provider-enumeration error text is replaced by a warning-icon->small-modal (icon shown only when errors exist; modal lists ProviderEnumerationError entries + lastError). Note the new default landing = Welcome screen (large logo + New conversation) rendered when no conversation is active, and that Conversations are nested under the Chat nav item. Preserve the existing Section 8.1 bullets about Enter/Shift+Enter and no-silent-no-op (they still hold).

Edit Section 8.2 (Model selector) to reflect that the routing-mode control and model picker now live INLINE in the composer (compact), that the rationale is an info icon, and that the enumeration errors surface via the warning-icon->modal near the composer (Diagnostics panel unchanged).

Add a new subsection (e.g. 8.1.x or a new 8.6 'Message context inputs: attachments, repository, web search') documenting: (a) ATTACH - native dialog via tauri-plugin-dialog; read_text_file / read_file_base64 commands; vision-capability gate for images with a visible unsupported notice; per-file + total byte caps; context prepended into the message content String; cleared after one turn. (b) REPOSITORY - list_repo_files with filtering (.git/node_modules/target/etc), entry cap + truncated flag, user selects a bounded subset within a total size cap. (c) WEB SEARCH - pluggable WebSearchProvider trait + WebSearchKind enum, Tavily default (with the rationale for choosing it), key stored via SecretStore under a stable handle and never returned across IPC, additive AppConfig.web_search, Settings 'Web Search' section, run_web_search command, composer 🌐 toggle, and the invariant that an unconfigured/failed search shows a visible non-fatal notice and still sends (no silent hang). Clearly flag web search as needing the user's key + live verification.

List every NEW command in the appropriate place (mirroring how existing commands are listed in Section 8): read_text_file, read_file_base64, list_repo_files, set_web_search_provider, get_web_search_config, clear_web_search_provider, run_web_search - each with its camelCase IPC shape and that it is registered in generate_handler! + has an IPC wrapper + a TS type.

Update the Section 9 security notes if needed: the web-search key follows the Section 9.1 keychain-by-reference invariant (plaintext in, only a SecretRef stored, resolved core-internally at search time, never crosses IPC); file reads are bounded/display-safe. If the coder recorded a secret-persistence follow-up (in-memory vs keychain), note it as a known issue / follow-up rather than a fix in this task.
If tasks.md has a natural place, add a short phase note referencing this task (optional, additive) - but do not restructure tasks.md.
Do NOT use em dashes in the prose. Match the existing spec's flat-prose style and heading conventions.
acceptance_criteria: architecture.md Section 8.1/8.2 describe the bottom-anchored composer with inline controls, the info-icon rationale, and the warning-icon->modal error UX, plus the Welcome screen + Chat-nested Conversations.
A subsection documents the concrete mechanism for attach, repository context, and web search (Tavily default + pluggable + Settings-configurable + keychain-stored key + visible non-fatal fallback).
Every new command is listed with its camelCase shape and its registration/IPC/type requirements noted.
Security notes cover the web-search key (keychain-by-reference) and bounded file reads; any secret-persistence follow-up is recorded as a known issue, not silently fixed.
Prose uses no em dashes and matches the existing spec style.
verification: Re-read the edited spec sections and confirm they accurately describe the shipped FEAT-002/003/004 behavior (cross-check against the actual code), that all new commands are listed, and that there are no em dashes.
Confirm the doc changes are consistent with the code (command names, capability-gate behavior, fallback-and-still-send invariant).
findings:
DONE (docs-only, committed onto feat/kiro-chat-redesign). Updated .kiro/specs/hybrid-orchestrator/architecture.md to be the accurate source of truth for what shipped on this branch. No product code changed. Every claim cross-checked against the real code (crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs generate_handler!, commands.rs, providers/src/web_search.rs + net_share.rs, persistence/src/config.rs, frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts + types/index.ts).

SECTIONS CHANGED:
- Section 8.1 (Chat interface): already carried the FEAT-002 redesign bullet (bottom-anchored composer, inline model + routing controls, 'Why this model?' info icon, Attach/Repository/Web-search toggle icons, Refresh icon, warning-icon->EnumerationErrorModal, Welcome-screen landing gated on activeConversationId, Conversations nested under the Chat nav item) plus the FEAT-003 attach/repo bullet (incl. the image-multimodal follow-up note) and the FEAT-004 web-search bullet. Left those intact (did not duplicate); only removed the three em dashes they contained (lines in the FEAT-002/FEAT-004 bullets) to keep the whole spec em-dash-free.
- Section 8.2 (Model selector): updated the Components line to 'grouped Network vs Local vs Cloud'; added a new 'Network peers grouped distinctly (FEAT-006)' bullet documenting the network-peer- id-prefix classification (Network first, no double-count under Local) and that peers enumerate/route via the existing load() path with no pipeline change.

NEW SUBSECTIONS ADDED:
- Section 8.6 'Message context inputs: attachments, repository, and web search': concrete mechanisms for ATTACH (tauri-plugin-dialog, read_text_file 256 KiB/UTF-8/binary-reject, read_file_base64 4 MiB + MIME + domain::file_context base64, vision gate + visible notice, chips, prepended into content, cleared after one turn, full multimodal a follow-up), REPOSITORY (list_repo_files skip-list .git/node_modules/target/dist/build/etc, MAX_REPO_ENTRIES=500 + truncated, 128 KiB total cap, per-file read_text_file), and WEB SEARCH (WebSearchProvider trait + WebSearchKind enum, Tavily default + rationale, configurable base_url for wiremock, SecretRef under 'web-search' handle, additive AppConfig.web_search, run_web_search, 🌐 toggle default OFF, unconfigured/failed -> visible role=status notice and STILL sends, live-verification user-only). ENDS with the full list of all 13 NEW commands, each with its camelCase IPC shape and the note that each is registered in generate_handler! + has an IPC wrapper + a TS type.
- Section 9.3.1 'Local network (LAN) model sharing': CONSUME (peer = GenericOpenAI ProviderConfig row, id network-peer-<hash>, enumerates/routes via existing path, add/list/remove_network_peer, check_provider_base_url posture blocks link-local/metadata + warns non-loopback plaintext, key as SecretRef, ProvidersChanged emit, wiremock proof); PRIVACY decision (peer is OFF-HOST, excluded from local_provider_ids so LocalOnly/Confidential never routes to a peer, pinned by test); SHARE (ModelShareServer seam, render_models_response GET /v1/models, try_bind visible Running/Unavailable status, shares only on-host local models, set/get_model_sharing, additive AppConfig.model_sharing default OFF port 11435, live binding user-only); DISCOVERY (PeerDiscovery trait + StubPeerDiscovery empty-without-error, discover_network_peers bounded timeout, non-fatal empty notice, real mDNS a follow-up); Settings 'Network Sharing' section + keychain-by-reference for the peer key.

SECTION 9 SECURITY UPDATES:
- 9.1: added a bullet noting the web-search key and any LAN peer key use the same SecretStore.store by-reference path; RECORDED the secret-persistence issue as a KNOWN ISSUE / follow-up (prod uses KeyringSecretStore so the write path IS the keychain; the 'no secret found for handle gemini-cloud' diagnostic is likely a handle-mismatch or evicted/cleared keychain entry across sessions, not an in-memory-store bug; NOT fixed in this task).
- 9.3: added a bullet that the web-search key follows the 9.1 keychain-by-reference invariant (plaintext in, only a SecretRef stored, resolved core-internally, never crosses IPC) and that attachment/repo file reads are bounded and display-safe.

Appendix A coverage table: added rows for Section 8.6 (message context inputs) and LAN model sharing (Sections 8.2, 9.3.1).

COMMAND LIST CONFIRMED: all 13 new commands are listed in Section 8.6 with correct camelCase IPC shapes and registration/IPC-wrapper/TS-type notes: read_text_file, read_file_base64, list_repo_files, set_web_search_provider, get_web_search_config, clear_web_search_provider, run_web_search, add_network_peer, list_network_peers, remove_network_peer, set_model_sharing, get_model_sharing, discover_network_peers. Verified each is present in crates/tauri-app/src/lib.rs generate_handler! (lines 74-105), has a wrapper in frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts, and a TS type in frontend/src/types/index.ts.

NO EM DASHES: grep for U+2014 across architecture.md returns 0 (removed the 3 pre-existing ones in the FEAT-002/FEAT-004 bullets). Prose matches the existing flat-prose bullet style. No build/test gate for a markdown-only change. Did NOT push/tag/PR; did NOT change any product code; did NOT restructure tasks.md (no natural additive place required).
